name: Crimson Nocturne Wuxia Print Montage / 绯夜武侠胶片拼贴

source_summary.provenance: Observed from three user-supplied vertical martial-arts poster references. Raw references, faces, copy, and watermarks are not stored.

visual_rules.medium_behavior: aged vertical martial-arts release-print and editorial photomontage appearance with controlled double exposure, distressed scan edges, and tactile analog reproduction
palette_logic: deep black owns the negative field and frame edges
crimson red owns the dominant face, fabric, or emotional pressure
cyan blue owns night water, distant silhouettes, or the secondary narrative layer
warm amber may bridge skin and red highlights
off-white is reserved for user-supplied vertical copy only
visual_rules.shape_line_language: one extreme cropped portrait mass, one much smaller narrative silhouette layer, diagonal occlusion or fabric/blade-like edge, soft photographic boundaries, and narrow vertical text columns when exact copy is supplied
texture_material_logic: coarse irregular print grain varies across shadow and midtone density
small scratches, dust, edge fogging, and light leaks remain sparse and nonuniform
faces retain skin texture beneath print softness rather than plastic polish
dark fabric and hair merge into black fields but keep local edge information
visual_rules.lighting_logic: low-key underexposure with a saturated crimson key or fabric reflection on the dominant portrait, cyan-blue secondary night light, localized warm flare, and no neutral commercial fill
composition_logic: dominant face or eye occupies roughly half to two-thirds of the vertical frame
secondary story appears as a small double-exposed silhouette, landscape, reflection, or lower panel
large black negative areas separate layers and preserve mystery
asymmetric margins and partial crops create pressure rather than centered poster symmetry
typography_logic: vertical Chinese copy uses restrained off-white or gray and generous tracking
small English subtitle may anchor a lower corner only when exact text is supplied
typography remains sparse and never becomes fake calligraphic clutter
visual_rules.optics_rendering_logic: locally soft focus, low-to-medium microcontrast, dense textured blacks, soft highlight shoulder, coarse uneven grain, mild crimson halation at bright edges, restrained bloom, subtle vignette, scan scratches, and occasional edge light leak
motifs: dominant portrait plus miniature narrative memory

inferred_traits: the visual system treats character memory and present danger as two exposure layers
analog degradation is expressive and deliberate rather than a universal quality defect
unknowns: exact film stock or scanning process
transfer_rules: transfer the dominant-portrait versus miniature-story hierarchy, not the source people or story
transfer red/cyan color ownership and analog print behavior while adapting copy, costume, and scene to the new brief
keep grain, halation, scratches, and light leaks intentionally uneven and subordinate to face/story readability
use vertical typography only when the user supplies exact copy
forbidden_transfer: source costume, jewelry, weapons, boats, landscape, or silhouettes
exact split points, crop coordinates, or layer arrangement
generic random scratches that hide the image

prompts: Transfer the style to an original contemporary jazz singer backstage after a failed performance, with no martial-arts content and no text.
Transfer the style to an original desert science-fiction courier remembering a lost orbital station, with a new silhouette layer and no source content.
validation.notes: Forward-tested on 2026-08-19 with two unrelated subjects using the same image generator. The jazz singer result preserved the dominant crimson portrait, cyan miniature story layer, deep black field, analog print texture, and double-exposure hierarchy without martial-arts content or copied text. The science-fiction courier result preserved the same transferable mechanisms while changing character, wardrobe, setting, and secondary narrative layer; no source face, costume, wording, signature, or watermark was reproduced. These are visual checks, not guarantees of exact repeatability.
